# Golden fixtures — AUTOSAR SWS requirement extraction

These are the frozen contract for document ingestion. Story **S1.3.4** creates
them; story **S1.3.3** (the requirement extractor) is measured against them at
**≥90 % recall**, and any later change to parsing or extraction must keep them
green or update them deliberately.

## Why there are no PDFs here

The AUTOSAR specifications are copyrighted, `data/` is gitignored, and
`CLAUDE.md` forbids committing the PDFs (controller ruling **R11**). So what is
committed is the **frozen parser output** for a handful of pages plus the
**hand-labeled** requirements for those same pages. Everything in this
directory therefore passes on a fresh clone with no `data/` directory, and the
parser's own mechanics are tested separately against a synthetic PDF built
in-test (`backend/tests/test_pdf_loader.py`).

## The files

| File | What it is | Regenerable? |
|---|---|---|
| `fixtures.json` | the frozen page list, with the reason each page was chosen | no — edited by hand |
| `<fixture>.blocks.json` | the parser's output for that page: page number, size, and every text block with its bbox and char span | **yes** — `regenerate.py` |
| `<fixture>.expected.json` | the requirements a correct extractor must produce for that page | **never** — hand-labeled ground truth |
| `regenerate.py` | rebuilds only the `.blocks.json` halves | — |

`.expected.json` was written by reading the rendered pages. It must **never**
be regenerated from code output: a fixture generated by the thing it is meant
to test proves nothing. If the extractor disagrees with a label, the default
assumption is that the extractor is wrong. Changing a label requires
re-reading the page and saying so in the commit message.

## The frozen pages, and why each one

| Fixture | Page | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `can_driver_p032` | CAN Driver 32 | 9 plain `[ID] ⌈text⌋(refs)` requirements — the ordinary case, at density |
| `can_driver_p043` | CAN Driver 43 | the **titled** variant (`SWS_Can_91019`, `SWS_Can_91020`), whose bodies are **tables**; also an upstream id split across a line break |
| `can_driver_p034` | CAN Driver 34 | `SWS_Can_00407` opens here — the **page-break** case: no single bbox, `char_span` only |
| `can_driver_p035` | CAN Driver 35 | closes `SWS_Can_00407`. Frozen as a **pair** with page 34; the furniture between the halves is what the cleaning pass must remove |
| `can_driver_p023` | CAN Driver 23 | the §6 Requirements-Tracing table: 33 bracketed `SWS_Can_*` ids and **zero** requirements — the false-positive guard |
| `can_interface_p034` | CAN Interface 34 | 7 requirements in the **other ID casing** (`SWS_CANIF_*`); both documents must be represented or a casing bug passes every test |
| `can_driver_p094` | CAN Driver 94 | `SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509/00510/00511` — the `_CONSTR_` infix, worth ~20 requirements corpus-wide |
| `can_nm_p050` | CAN NM 50 | the fifth document (`SWS_CanNm_*`); two **titled** API definitions (`SWS_CanNm_00211`, `SWS_CanNm_00213`) whose bodies are whole **service tables**, interleaved with plain requirements; `SWS_CanNm_00213` closes with `⌋() ()` — a stray extra empty parens pair |
| `com_p117` | COM 117 | the largest document (209 pp); 5 plain + 1 **titled table** requirement (`SWS_Com_00346`), all with upstream `(SRS_Com_02037)`; the cross-module symbol `PduR_ComTransmit`, and `ComIPduCallout`-style config parameters the symbol pattern must ignore |
| `pdu_router_p060` | PDU Router 60 | `SWS_PDUR_00816` — the document's one **UPPERCASE**-cased id, next to the normal-cased `SWS_PduR_00100`; a `req_id_pattern` without the `PDUR` alternative drops it while every other fixture stays green. Both are titled table bodies (`"Definiton"`, sic) |

Ten files for nine distinct cases: the page-break case inherently costs two
pages (controller ruling **R15**). The last three joined on 2026-08-27 with
the CanNm/Com/PduR documents, so every ingested document is represented. Do
not trim the set to hit a round number.

## `.blocks.json` format

```
fixture, document_key, source_document, source_sha256, corpus_version
page (1-based), page_count, width, height, char_start, char_end
parser: { library, version, extraction_mode, module }
blocks: [ { block_no, bbox: [x0,y0,x1,y1], char_start, char_end, text } ]
```

`extraction_mode` is `"blocks"` — PyMuPDF's `page.get_text("blocks")`. The
`char_start`/`char_end` offsets are into the **whole document's** text, which
`ingestion.pdf_loader` defines as the concatenation of every block's text in
extraction order; that is why page 35's `char_start` equals page 34's
`char_end`, and why `SWS_Can_00407`'s span is expressible at all. Block text
is verbatim and newline-terminated — page furniture included, because removing
it is the extractor's job, not the parser's.

## `.expected.json` format and the text-normalization contract

```
fixture, document_key, source_document, page, labeled, notes
requirements: [ { id, title, text, upstream_ids, named_symbols,
                  page, spans_page_break } ]
```

* `id` — verbatim from the document, **casing preserved**
  (`SWS_Can_00011` vs. `SWS_CANIF_00001`).
* `title` — the text between `]` and `⌈` in the titled variant, else `null`.
  Source typos are transcribed verbatim (`"Definiton"`, sic).
* `text` — the body between `⌈` and `⌋`, normalized as below.
* `upstream_ids` — the `(…)` list after the closing `⌋`, matching
  `(?:SRS|RS)_[A-Za-z]+_\d+`. Ids referenced inside the body are **not**
  upstream ids.
* `named_symbols` — `extract_named_symbols()` over the normalized body: every
  match of the manifest's `symbol_pattern`, first-appearance order,
  deduplicated. Asserted for **completeness**, not just correctness — the
  labeled list must equal that function's output exactly.
* `spans_page_break` — `true` when the body crosses a page boundary, i.e. the
  case where `Requirement.bbox` must be `None` and `char_span` is the only
  usable locator. Such a requirement is labeled on the page **its id appears
  on**, exactly once, and never again on the continuation page.

### The normalization contract lives in code, not here

The labeled `text` assumes the normalization defined by
**`backend/ingestion/text_norm.py`**, which is the single source of truth —
its module docstring is the spec, and it is ratified as binding on the
extractor (S1.3.3/D4). **Call `normalize_requirement_text()`; do not
reimplement it.** `test_golden_fixtures.py` imports that same function and
asserts every labeled `text` is found verbatim in the frozen page output, so a
transcription slip or a divergent reimplementation fails the suite.

Two details of that contract are easy to get wrong from a prose summary, so
they are stated here as well — but the module, not this file, is authoritative:

* a `footer_patterns` match is replaced with a **single newline `"\n"`**, not
  deleted. The patterns are anchored on the newlines around the furniture, and
  pattern 1 consumes the newline that pattern 2 needs to match the following
  page's header. Deleting instead of substituting leaves the page-35 header in
  the text and fuses `driver.Specification` — it breaks the p034/p035 pair.
* a `drop_markers` occurrence (`▽`, `△`) is replaced with a **single space**,
  not deleted, so a marker between two words cannot fuse them. (No fixture
  distinguishes the two today — the markers occur only on p023, which has no
  labeled text — hence stating it explicitly.)

Nothing else is removed: bullet markers (`•`), the source's curly apostrophes
(`’`), hyphens that were not at a line break, and the source's own spelling
mistakes all survive verbatim.

## Regenerating the `.blocks.json` halves

```
cd backend
uv run python -m ingestion.run ../projects/autosar-can/project.yaml --stop-after docs   # once
uv run python tests/fixtures/golden/regenerate.py
```

Run this only for a deliberate parser or PyMuPDF upgrade, and **review the
diff** — a change here is a change in what every downstream stage sees. The
`source_sha256` in each file records which PDF the output came from; if it
changes, AUTOSAR republished the document and the hand labels need re-reading
too.
